title: The Krell Transformation Rule
teaches: Understanding the core definition: swap coordinates and increment the second value.
visual: A Cartesian grid appears with axes labeled x and y. A point P at (3, 5) is highlighted in blue. An arrow points to a new position where the coordinates are swapped to (5, 3), then the y-coordinate increments by 1 to become 4, landing on Q(5, 4). Labels 'Swap' and '+1' appear sequentially above the transformation.
narration: A Krell step transforms any grid point (x, y) into a new location. First, we swap the coordinates to get (y, x), then we add 1 to the second number, resulting in (y, x + 1).

title: Grid Point Validity
teaches: Confirming that Krell steps always result in valid integer grid points.
visual: The animation shows a generic point (x, y) on the grid. As it undergoes the Krell step, the resulting point (y, x+1) snaps precisely onto an intersection of the grid lines. A checkmark appears next to the text 'Always lands on a grid point'.
narration: Because we start with integers and only perform swapping and addition, every Krell step always lands exactly on another valid grid point.

title: The Staircase Path from Origin
teaches: Visualizing the specific sequence of points generated by repeating steps from (0, 0).
visual: Starting at origin (0, 0), a path is drawn step-by-step: first to (0, 1), then to (1, 1), then to (1, 2), and finally to (2, 2). Each point is labeled with its coordinates as the line connects them, forming a jagged staircase shape.
narration: Repeating Krell steps from the origin creates a distinct staircase pattern. The path climbs through these specific points: (0,0) to (0,1), then (1,1), (1,2), and finally (2,2).

title: The Double Step Identity
teaches: Demonstrating that two consecutive Krell steps equal a diagonal shift of (+1, +1).
visual: A point A at (x, y) is shown. An arrow labeled 'Step 1' leads to an intermediate point. A second arrow labeled 'Step 2' leads to point B. Simultaneously, a dashed arrow directly from A to B shows the net result: moving right by 1 and up by 1. The label '(x+1, y+1)' appears at point B.
narration: Two consecutive Krell steps have a powerful simplification. Regardless of the starting position, two steps always move the point diagonally to (x + 1, y + 1).
